To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reduction of benzoqui-none by osmium(IV) complexes containing N-, S-, or P-donor ligands occurs by parallel pH-independent and pH-dependent pathways, the pH-independent pathway involves proton transfer from water to the osmium complex, and the pH-dependent pathway involves proton transfer to the benzoquinone.
the reduction of quinone (Q) by Os(IV) sulfilimido and hydrazido complexes occurs by parallel pH-independent and pH-dependent pathways.

the reactions of [Os(IV)L(Cl)(2)](+) complexes with benzoquinone in CH(3)OH/H(2)OH(2)O proceed via a H-bonding intermediate that is stabilized by the formation of a hydrogen bond to the quinone oxygen atom.

understanding the factors that control the reactivity and selectivity of metal-based redox catalysts for organic transformations, with an emphasis on reactions of relevance to biological systems.

the development of new synthetic methods, the characterization of the products of reactions, and the elucidation of mechanisms of organic and inorganic reactions, especially those that involve the transfer of hydrogen or electrons.

the development of new synthetic strategies to prepare and isolate new osmium complexes, the investigation of their reactivities, and the development of new catalytic systems for the oxidation and reduction of organic substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinetic isotope effects observed are consistent with the involvement of a hydride intermediate in the reduction of quinones by these Os(IV) complexes.
the observed isotope effects are consistent with proton transfer occurring in the rate-determining step of the pH-independent pathways.

the proton-coupled reduction of Q by [Os(IV)(N(R)(2))(2)(tpy)](+), [Os(IV) (NS(H)R)(2)(tpy)(+)](+), and [Os(IV)-NP(H)(2)(Et)(2)](2+) complexes occurs by an outer-sphere electron-transfer process that is coupled with a proton-transfer step.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the magnitude of the observed kinetic isotope effects is a function of the strength of the Os-N, Os-S, or Os-P bond, the strength of the H-bond between the proton donor atom and the proton acceptor, and the strength of the O-H bond in H(2)Q.
proton transfer in the transition state is concerted with electron transfer, but that the proton transfer step is not rate-limiting.
the magnitude of the KIE for a given reaction is dependent on the nature of the proton donor and the nature of the electron acceptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnitude of the isotope effect depends not only on the proton donor atom but also on the nature of the metal center.
the kinetic isotope effects observed are much greater than the corresponding equilibrium isotope effects.

the magnitude of the kinetic isotope effect for proton-coupling in a reaction is not determined by the nature of the proton donor but rather by the relative energies of the reactant, transition state, and product.
